skill.name: memory-management
skill.description: Manages cross-session marketing memory for SEO, influencer, paid ads, email, launch, social, and narrative work. It organizes hot cache, active files, archives, consolidation, and privacy cleanup.
skill.summary: Keeps campaign memory current, scoped, and privacy-aware across AI sessions.

security_audit.summary: Reviewed 87 static findings and found them to be documentation false positives. The alerts are Markdown links, code fences, file paths, metadata URLs, or bounded maintenance examples; no automatic execution, data exfiltration, or prompt injection was found. The skill modifies local memory files by design, so users should still confirm privacy purge changes before edits.

remediation.issue: Command-like examples can be misread as executable behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Label shell snippets as illustrative and keep user confirmation before any purge action.

remediation.issue: Privacy purge actions modify local memory files by design.
remediation.suggestion: Continue showing matched files before edits and document that git history requires separate user action.

content.user_title: Manage Marketing Memory Across AI Sessions
content.value_statement: Marketing projects lose important context when audits, campaigns, and decisions spread across sessions. This skill organizes hot cache, active memory, archives, and privacy cleanup in a disciplined lifecycle.
actual_capabilities: Initializes a marketing memory structure for new projects.
Maintains hot cache, warm files, and cold archives.
Promotes, demotes, and archives campaign facts by documented rules.
Runs memory hygiene checks for size, age, and frontmatter fields.
Consolidates duplicate or conflicting memory entries with supersession notes.
Guides confirmed GDPR and CCPA working-tree purge records.
limitations: It does not score content, domains, ads, emails, launches, or narratives.
It does not erase data from git history or external systems.
It needs user confirmation before destructive privacy purge actions.
It depends on available project files and user-provided context.

use_cases.title: Preserve Campaign Context
use_cases.description: Keep priorities, competitors, keywords, offers, and decisions available across repeated AI sessions.

use_cases.title: Clean Stale Memory
use_cases.description: Review hot cache size, stale entries, archive candidates, and missing memory frontmatter.

use_cases.title: Handle Privacy Requests
use_cases.description: Find subject mentions, confirm scope, anonymize or delete working-tree memory, and record the purge.

prompt_templates.title: Start Project Memory
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new marketing project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up marketing memory for a new project. Ask for the minimum context needed, create the memory plan, and list files you would update.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh Hot Cache
prompt_templates.scenario: Update active context after a new analysis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refresh the hot cache with these new campaign findings. Show promoted items, archived details, and any open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Archive Stale Items
prompt_templates.scenario: Review memory health before a report.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a memory hygiene check. List hot-cache size issues, stale files, missing frontmatter, and recommended archive actions.

prompt_templates.title: Consolidate Conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a consolidation pass across hot cache and relevant candidates. Deduplicate facts, supersede stale conflicts, and park ambiguity in open loops.

output_examples.input: Run a memory health check before the monthly report.
output: Hot cache is within the line limit but has two entries older than 30 days.
Three warm files need frontmatter updates.
Recommended action is to archive completed campaigns and refresh stale metrics.

output_examples.input: Save the latest domain audit results for future sessions.
output: The audit summary is ready for the monthly audit archive.
Two durable findings should be promoted to hot cache after user approval.
Detailed scoring should remain in the audit folder.

output_examples.input: Purge mentions of a data subject from memory.
output: Matched memory files are listed for confirmation first.
After confirmation, the working tree can be anonymized or deleted by scope.
The purge log records a redacted label and notes that git history is separate.

best_practices: Confirm destructive purge choices before editing memory files.
Keep hot cache under the documented line and size limits.
Separate user-approved decisions from inferred notes.
anti_patterns: Treating old archive facts as current without a refresh.
Saving third-party personal data without a lawful basis when privacy law applies.
Overwriting approved decisions during consolidation instead of surfacing conflicts.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages project memory for marketing work, including hot cache, active files, archives, decisions, and purge records.

faq.question: Does it write marketing content?
faq.answer: No. It stores and organizes memory. Use the relevant writer or auditor skill for content work.

faq.question: Does it delete files automatically?
faq.answer: No. The purge flow requires matched files, a user choice, and confirmation before changes.

faq.question: Can it remove data from git history?
faq.answer: No. It only edits the working tree and explains that git history cleanup is separate.

faq.question: Can it work without connected marketing tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It can ask for user-provided keywords, competitors, metrics, campaigns, and terminology.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible skill hosts.
